elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment or minimum-volume requirement.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer commits to purchase “no minimum amount,” and Section 12.3 confirms that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer pays fees only for Services ordered or used.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly provides that Customer “pays only for Services ordered or used.”

elements.element: Any minimum commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No minimum commitment exists under the rendered language, so the condition requiring a 12-month limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any minimum commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No minimum commitment exists to be reduced, so the condition requiring a 30-day reduction right is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any commitment shortfall is resolved through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Because there is no minimum commitment, there can be no commitment shortfall, penalty, or need for a true-up mechanism.

result.reason: The redline fully reaches the preferred position by eliminating the minimum purchase obligation and limiting payment to ordered or used Services. It also satisfies the fallback protections because their triggering condition—a minimum commitment—is absent. The amendment is limited to the relevant commitment language and remains consistent with Section 12.3. Drafting quality is reduced by the awkward and unnecessary phrase “commits to purchase no minimum amount ... in each of the next three years”; a cleaner formulation would simply state that Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
